original_question: Let T013(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and all three bone orientations are allowed. Whenever the Conway-Lagarias invariant of the (a,b)-benzel is negative or zero, must a type-013 tiling exist?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4 ("Left stones, three kinds of bones"): whether every (a,b)-benzel whose Conway-Lagarias invariant is negative or zero admits a type-013 tiling. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target: it identifies the correct tiling type 013, correctly interprets that type as allowing left stones and forbidding right stones while allowing all three bone orientations, and asks the right existential question conditioned on the sign of the Conway-Lagarias invariant. That is exactly the content of Problem 4. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
missing_details: It does not state the parameter range for the benzel. In the paper, the (a,b)-benzel is defined for positive integers a,b satisfying 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

It does not define the (a,b)-benzel itself. The paper defines it geometrically as the union of unit hexagonal cells fully contained in a specific hexagon in the standard hexagonal grid, described using the complex numbers 1, ω, and ω^2 with ω = e^{2πi/3}. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

It does not make explicit that the allowed tiles are translates of the prototiles, and that in type 013 the permitted prototiles are exactly the left stone and the three bones: vertical, rising, and falling. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

It does not sharpen the existential claim into the paper’s counting notation. Since T013(a,b) is a counting function, the existence statement should be stated as T013(a,b) > 0. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

It does not define the Conway-Lagarias invariant in the paper’s terms. The paper recalls that for stones-and-bones tilings it is the total area of right stones minus the total area of left stones, and then gives a piecewise explicit formula for the (a,b)-benzel. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

It leaves implicit, by the formulas in Section 1, that the hypothesis I(a,b) <= 0 can only occur when a+b ≡ 0 (mod 3): when a+b ≡ 1 (mod 3), the invariant equals the benzel area and is positive, and when a+b ≡ 2 (mod 3), the invariant is also positive. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

It does not make the universal quantifier explicit. The paper asks whether the implication holds for every valid (a,b)-benzel, not merely for the small values displayed in Table 3. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
refined_question: Let ω = e^{2πi/3}. For positive integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, let the (a,b)-benzel be the union of the unit hexagonal cells fully contained in the hexagon with vertices aω+b, -aω^2-b, aω^2+bω, -a-bω, a+bω^2, and -aω-bω^2. Let T013(a,b) be the number of tilings of this benzel by translates of the left stone together with the three bones (vertical, rising, and falling), with right stones forbidden. If I(a,b) denotes the Conway-Lagarias invariant of the (a,b)-benzel, given by I(a,b) = (3a^2-6ab+3b^2-a-b)/2 when a+b ≡ 0 (mod 3), I(a,b) = (-a^2+4ab-b^2-a-b+2)/2 when a+b ≡ 1 (mod 3), and I(a,b) = (3a^2-6ab+3b^2+a+b-2)/2 when a+b ≡ 2 (mod 3), is it true that T013(a,b) > 0 whenever I(a,b) <= 0? ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s exact Problem 4, not a neighboring conjecture. Section 1 introduces benzels, the five prototiles, the notation T_{ijk}(a,b), and the explicit Conway-Lagarias invariant for benzels. Section 4 then specializes to the case of left stones with all three bones, observes that positive invariant rules out such tilings, notes that the computed table entries are positive when the invariant is nonpositive, and asks precisely whether type-013 tilings always exist in that regime. The refined version only makes those definitions and quantifiers explicit so that the question becomes fully stand-alone without broadening it. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
